scope: Surviving Victorian red-brick engine house and its connected one-storey boiler house at Western Springs, with hipped roofs, basalt quoins, tall round-headed windows, and large boiler-room arches.
geometryBasis: The mapped common south wall and north-side step constrain the 25.9 m connected envelope. The deeper eastern volume is the two-storey engine house. The western volume is the single-storey boiler wing.
sectionBasis: The heritage records identify red brick, dressed basalt quoins and openings, round-arched multi-pane windows, cornices, entrance steps, hipped roofs, and broad arched boiler-house doorways.
next: Model the linked Victorian engine house and boiler wing at the present-day footprint.
